title: ALMA Observations of Quasar Host Galaxies at z ≃ 4.8
question: What are the host galaxy properties (dust, dynamical and gas masses, SFR, companions, [C II]-Mg II offsets) of luminous z~4.8 quasars, split into Herschel-detected (FIR-bright) and undetected (FIR-faint)?

what.value: Mg II-based redshifts, black hole masses and bolometric luminosities

evidence.quote: Black Hole masses were taken from T11 and are based on Mg II measurements.
values and errors from N14, with the 250 $\mu$m flux error corrected as explained above

what.value: Six quasars from pilot sample, ALMA measurements

evidence.quote: Previously, in T17, we observed three FIR-bright, and three FIR-faint quasar from our sample using ALMA.
we also list the SDSS-based redshift determinations published in (cite: Hewett_2010)

what.value: Literature [CII]-Mg II offsets for z>~6 quasars compilation

external_data.citation: Decarli2018, Willott 2013/2015/2017, Venemans 2012/2016/2017, Mazzucchelli2017, Banados2015, Wang2016

recipe.method: CLEAN with Briggs weighting; continuum from line-free spw pair; UVCONTSUB on [CII] pair

recipe.goal: Measure continuum and [CII] fluxes and sizes
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fits to continuum and zero-moment images (spatial); 1D spectral Gaussian fits as check; aperture photometry for J1447
Velocity offsets between [CII] and Mg II (and SDSS) redshifts; compile with literature quasars
Fit Chary&Elbaz, Magnelli SMG, and gray-body SEDs to ALMA (+Herschel) photometry; integrate 8-1000 micron; SFR = L_FIR/1e10
assumptions: FIR emission dominated by SF-heated dust; Chabrier IMF

recipe.method: Optically thin dust: Md = S D_L^2 / (kappa B(T))
Mdyn = 9.8e8 D FWHM^2/sin^2 i; dispersion-dominated alternative; Mgas = 100 x Mdust
Adopt Mstar = 0.4 Mdyn (fgas=0.6); compare SFR-Mstar with Schreiber2015/Tomczak2016 MS; compute MBH/Mstar and growth rates over 50 Myr with eta=0.1

answer_key.quantity: Mean Mg II blueshift relative to [CII] (17 hosts)

evidence.quote: The average value for $\Delta v_{{\rm Mg}\,\textsc{ii} }$ is 464 km s$^{-1}$, with a standard deviation of 657 km s$^{-1}$
while the median is found to be at 379 km s$^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: Mean offset in compilation incl. literature

evidence.quote:
we found a mean $z_{\left[{\rm C}\,\textsc{ii}\right] }
- z_{{\rm Mg}\,\textsc{ii} }$ of 372 km s$^{-1}$

with dust masses of $10^{9.0}$ and $10^{8.4}
M_{\odot}$, respectively
our total observed sample of 18 quasars has 5 sources with companions
We find a mean $M_{BH}/M_{\star}$ ratio of 1/19
OS values have a range of 0.005” - 0.062” for our entire sample.
